newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed, spot month slumps.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed, spot month slumps.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed on Friday with spot December retreating on trade and producer selling, floor sources said.

The board headed lower at the open on news that the Colombian truckers' strike had ended after 11 days. But local buying lifted December off early lows and brought the back months above unchanged, traders said.
Today's activity lopped 1.90 cents off December's premium to second-position March, but its margin remained steep at 11.90 cents.
December ended down 1.45 cents, at 116.00, after ranging between 117.30 and 115.35. Second-month March rose 0.45 cent, to 104.10, while the rest closed 0.20 to 1.35 higher.

The head of the National Federation of Coffee Growers said Friday coffee shipments to Colombia's ports returned to normal this morning, after representatives of striking truck drivers signed an agreement Thursday with the government to end the strike.

However, Jorge Cardenas said delays could still be expected in Colombia's October coffee shipments, with about 150,000 60-kilo bags promised for delivery this month unlikely to reach roasters until November.
Volume was relatively light at an estimated 6,402 lots, slightly lower than Thursday's official tally of 6,905 lots.
